subject: Control/Data topology alignment + deployment assembly
messages:
From: Soliton Infra <infraops@soliton.ai>
To: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deploy - control/data interface and egress question

Hi Elliot / Marissa,

Thanks again for the kickoff yesterday. We're starting the network design for our Soliton pilot (private VPC with colocated inference nodes) and have two asks to validate before we start provisioning:

1) Control plane API surface — we need a clear list of ports/protocols and a simple schematic showing how the customer control plane (in our VPC) will reach Redwood control plane components vs which paths stay entirely on the data plane.
2) Egress and audit expectations — our security team requires confirmation that inference outbound traffic (telemetry/metrics only) will be NAT'd through our edge and that any call-home is limited to cert-validated endpoints. They also want to see KMS keyflow for model fetches (notes on where keys live and who rotates them).

Can you provide a short reference schematic and a deploy checklist we can hand to our colo team? Prefer PDFs + a checklist spreadsheet if possible.

Attachments: none (so far)

Appreciate it — we want to lock this down by end of week so procurement can finish rack orders.

— Diego (Infra)
Soliton AI
infraops@soliton.ai

From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.com>
To: Soliton Infra <infraops@soliton.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy - control/data interface and egress question

Diego — thanks, got it. High-level answers first, then attachments and next steps.

Quick answers
- Control plane: authenticated HTTPS (mTLS optional) on port 443 to our control-plane endpoints (control.redwood.com). We surface a management API and agent bootstrap endpoint; agent-to-control uses short-lived certs.
- Data plane: inference traffic stays within your VPC / colocation fabric and connects to the dedicated runtime over L2/L3 peering or private interconnect; no control calls are embedded in per-request datapath.
- Egress: telemetry and metrics are buffered and forwarded to our telemetry collectors over TLS to a single allowed egress IP range (we provide CIDR). If you require NAT through your edge, that is supported; we just need the SNAT mapping for audit logs.
- KMS / model fetch: Model artifacts can be stored in your customer bucket; we support integrating with your KMS (customer-managed keys). Our agent requests temporary tokens to fetch the model; keys never leave your key store.

I've attached a reference schematic and an ops checklist to hand to colo/NOC: vpc-control-data-topology-v2.pdf (diagram), ops-deploy-checklist.xlsx (preflight + post-deploy verification), dataplane-egress-diagram.png (NAT and telemetry paths). Also linking the internal design note: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cExampleTopology

Action items
- Diego: confirm whether you want mTLS enforced for the control plane or if token-based mutual auth is sufficient (we can ship with token-based to start).
- Diego: confirm whether telemetry must exit via your NAT or if our managed egress is acceptable. If NAT, provide the source IP mappings.
- Kimberly/Mina: please review the ops checklist and flag anything missing for your side; I'll collect SRE runbook edits.

Inline quick notes in the attached PDF call out two optional patterns: 1) pinned control-plane ACLs by CIDR (recommended for production), 2) service mesh sidecar for tenants with stringent isolation (opt-in).

Thanks — I can hop on a 30-minute call today at 4pm PT if that helps.

— Elliot
Sr Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
elliot.price@redwood.com

Attachments:
- vpc-control-data-topology-v2.pdf (diagram)
- ops-deploy-checklist.xlsx (checklist)
- dataplane-egress-diagram.png (egress NAT + telemetry paths)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.com>
Cc: Soliton Infra <infraops@soliton.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 14:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy - control/data interface and egress question

Elliot / Diego — quick ops validation from my side after skimming the attachments.

1) Ops checklist: please add a short acceptance test for prefix caching behavior and KV cache boundaries. Customer infra teams often accidentally NAT _per-pod_ egress which breaks cache affinity; we need an item that verifies per-node sticky SNAT is preserved for a test run.

2) KMS flow: mine & Mina's recommendation is to record the key rotation schedule in the checklist and include a sample key-rotation playbook (where Redwood signals a rotate and customer performs KMS ops). I've added a small template row in ops-deploy-checklist.xlsx (row: KMS-rotate-protocol).

3) Observability: add a telemetry endpoint allowlist for your SOC. We will provide a CIDR range and certificate thumbprint; request Diego to confirm his SOC can pin that.

Inline comment (from Diego's point):
> Our security team requires confirmation that inference outbound traffic (telemetry/metrics only) will be NAT'd through our edge and that any call-home is limited to cert-validated endpoints.

Response: We support NAT through your edge. For cert validation we recommend mTLS and pinning cert thumbprints; token-based auth alone is acceptable for early pilots but plan for mTLS in production.

4) One more ask — please confirm whether your colo team can add a static route for our management CIDR to your dedicated interconnect. That simplifies ACLs on their side.

I'll attach a short runbook blurb for acceptance tests; Kimberly / Mina — can you add any additional SRE runbook steps?

— Marissa
Head of Deployments, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Thanks — this is exactly what we needed.

We confirmed with SOC: they will accept the pinned CIDR + cert thumbprint model. We prefer mTLS for the control plane in production; token-based auth ok for the pilot. We'll provide the SNAT mappings by EOD tomorrow and have opened NETOPS-1287 (https://jira.redwood.com/browse/NETOPS-1287) to track the network changes.

Can we take the 4pm PT slot to review the diagram with your SREs? Diego is available, and our colo lead will join. I've added an Acme contact for cross-team visibility — they are our collocation provider for the test rack.
